title: encode() does not validate that mode fits in 3 octal digits — mode > 0o777 produces malformed begin line
description: uuencoding/src/encode.rs encode() formats the mode as '{:03o}' (line 22). If a caller passes mode=0o1755 (setuid+sticky bits, a valid Unix mode), the begin line becomes 'begin 1755 filename\n' — 4 digits, which most decoders handle, but the format spec says 3. More importantly, mode=0xFFFFFFFF would emit 'begin 37777777777 filename\n' — an 11-digit octal string. The function doc says '3-digit octal' but does not enforce it. This is a silent footgun: the function accepts u32 freely but the output format is not defined for values > 0o7777.
acceptance_criteria: Either document that values > 0o7777 produce multi-digit mode strings (and specify that is intentional and decoders should handle it), or clamp/mask to 12 bits (0o7777) with a doc note, or return a Result. At minimum, test mode=0o1755 and mode=0xFFFFFFFF.
close_reason: Documented mode formatting behavior in encode(); added tests for mode=0o1755 and mode=0xFFFFFFFF
